# Phase D intent

[PRD v2.0](../../prd/sc-runtime-prd.md) is the product intent and top authority.
Its storage and writer requirements (PRD-STO-1–5), cron requirements
(PRD-CRON-1–5), command pattern, engineering rules (including PRD-ENG-5/6)
and deferred decisions apply directly. This document adds only the Phase D
delta; it does not restate or override those requirements.

The executable plan is Beads epic `run-phase-d`, indexed by
[phase-d.jsonl](../phase-d.jsonl). [Anchors](anchors.md) retain approved
constraints and their verbatim provenance. The earlier Markdown plan and the
three-sprint/eight-anchor status are historical.

## Phase D delta

**Adoption.** Unblock beads-cache's SQLite security upgrade and make the fixed
SDK usable from the registry. Acceptance includes the actual upstream migration
PR open with CI green at a recorded revision against the published release,
without local path, patch or Git SDK substitutes. Generated application
acceptance follows the PRD and live sprint criteria; the superseded vulnerable
SQLx-SQLite configuration is not an accepted Phase D outcome (PRD-STO-2/3;
PRD-CRON-3).

**Dependency choice and recommendations.** Published/template registry requirements
use tested floors with no upper bound (ANC-037). Consumers may pin what they want.
The template ships a recommended Cargo.lock at the newest tested combination;
.sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json records those versions for reference and
future revert/upgrade tools (ANC-038). The normal build and test suites check the selected versions.

**Release.** The recorded owner decision is coordinated **0.3.0** across nine
crates: `sc-storage`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-config`, `sc-transport`,
`sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-cron`, `sc-cron-commands` and `sc-monty` (owner
2026-11-12 requirement change item 1 adds the ninth crate; original version message
01M76S6D7T58E4CMKHJRCXFJ1J; `run-phase-d` release metadata). This supersedes
the earlier 0.2.1 target. The live plan owns package, advisory, integration and
consumer proof; this document claims no implementation or publication pass.

## Planning handover provenance

The user stated on 2026-11-11:

> The intention of phase-d is to make sc-runtime easy for consumers to use.
> today beads-cache is blocked because of the security warning on rusqlite.
> we need to be following 'best practices' for a scaffolding framework which does not block consumers from building or upgrading dependencies w/ non-breaking changes/upgrades.

Final owner approval uses the HTML diff after independent review. Historical
calibration packets and run evidence retain their original inputs.

records.statement: The sprint text MUST state a reason for each cron command that does not go through the shared command path.
records.scope: plan items that change cron commands, sc-cron-commands or the shared command path

pass: Cron run-now does not use the shared path because it writes no schedule row; the sprint says so.
fail: Cron stop is handled outside the shared path with no reason given.

records.quote: Name which cron commands go through the shared path; for any that do not, state the reason in the sprint text.
records.summary: reason stated for cron commands off the path
records.deterministic_check: each cron command listed off the shared path has a reason in the sprint text
records.check: each cron command listed off the shared path has a reason in the sprint text

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.
criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out, preserve, or plan for the directive given in `anchor.statement`? Look for the directive's specific content being present in the item: the same starting point, the same method, the same constraint, or an explicit step that does what the statement asks. A generic mention of the topic without the directive's specific content does not count. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.yes: The item text contains the directive's specific content, in its own words or the user's, as a step, constraint, or stated starting point.
criteria.no: The item text is silent about the directive: it neither includes the directive's specific content nor references it.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive itself is included.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
